Description: A massive retail mall redevelopment plan in Gaithersburg that would include life sciences space faces a pivotal city council vote Dec. 4. Plans for the roughly $1.24 billion, 3.6 million square foot redevelopment of the vacant Lakeforest Mall at 701 Russell Ave. have been in the works for several years. The owner, Mount Pleasant, S.C.-based WRS Inc. Real Estate Investments, has proposed a redevelopment of the existing, roughly 100-acre property into a multi-use employment, retail, residential and entertainment destination. The Gaithersburg City Council is scheduled to vote on a proposed new ordinance that would authorize it to negotiate early-vesting deals, called Development Rights and Responsibilities Agreements (DRRAs). The measure would clear the way for a potential deal to lock in development rights for the project earlier than usual, allowing WRS to raze the existing, 1 million square foot mall sooner than planned, by spring or summer 2024. That would begin clearing the way for up to 1,600 new residential units, 750,000 square feet of new commercial space – including life sciences and light manufacturing space – and 470,000 square feet of new retail.

Keystone Development + Investment has secured a $265.2 million loan from Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America (TIAA) affiliate Nuveen Real Estate, to expand the life science conversion of landmark former publishing headquarters The Curtis in Philadelphia. Part of the funding will be used for infrastructure upgrades and leasing costs at The Curtis, and another portion is intended to enable Keystone to convert the next 200,000 square feet at The Curtis to cGMP (current Good Manufacturing Practices) and research laboratories over the next several years.

Description: New York City's economic development arm will invest $50 million to expand the life science lab space at BioBAT at the Brooklyn Army Terminal, as part of a broader $1 billion investment to foster the biotech industry here. "These funds will enable BioBAT to build additional research labs and manufacturing space for successful companies," said Eva Cramer, president of BioBAT and vice president for biotechnology and scientific affairs at SUNY Downstate Health Sciences University, in a statement. "This will provide high-quality jobs and exciting medical innovations for our community." BioBAT occupies 245,100 square feet. About 40,000 square feet of that is leased by 10 tenants, with about 100,000 square feet remaining for improvement. The rest of the space is used for common areas and infrastructure. The expansion will add about 85,000 square feet of improved space ready for occupancy and the additional required infrastructure. The New York City Economic Development Corp. expects design will start in early 2022 for the project. The organization will follow its procurement processes for bringing on design and construction firms.

Construction SF: Plans for a new life science campus through the acquisition and redevelopment of the Shoreway Innovation Center in Belmont are underway following a serious financial commitment from real estate firm CBRE Group. CBRE announced Wednesday it had arranged $75 million in financing for the acquisition and redevelopment of Shoreway Innovation Center for the borrower, Four Corners Properties, a San Francisco Bay Area real estate company. According to CBRE, the 7-acre property at 1301 Shoreway Road will be redeveloped into a new life sciences campus, likely featuring the construction of two Class A life science buildings, approximately 500,000 to 600,000 aggregate square feet. It will include a multistory parking structure for around 1,500 spaces. The 6.9-acre site is southeast of Ralston and Highway 101. The proposed project would consist of approximately 542,035 square feet in total of life sciences development in two buildings. Building 1 is proposed at 8 stories (145 feet tall) and Building 2 is proposed at 7 stories (131 feet tall). Approximately 1,626 parking spaces would be provided in a nine-level parking garage and surface parking.

Genesis Marina is a 570,000 square foot life science campus located in Brisbane, California. The project consists of three buildings and a parking structure. The campus is designed to meet the needs of life science companies of all sizes, from early-stage startups to established pharmaceutical companies. The project is being developed by Phase 3 Real Estate Partners and built by Webcor Builders.

The 105 by Breakthrough is a 263,000 square foot lab and office building located in the Seaport District of Boston. The building is fully leased to CRISPR Therapeutics. The project features state-of-the-art lab space, a fitness center, and a rooftop terrace.

Torrey View by Breakthrough is a 10-acre life science campus located in the Del Mar Heights submarket of San Diego. The project will consist of three buildings totaling 520,000 square feet. The campus is designed to foster collaboration and innovation, with outdoor workspaces, a conference center, and a fitness center. The project is pre-leased to Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD).

300 Third is a six-story, 130,000 square foot laboratory and office building located in Kendall Square, Cambridge. The building is fully leased to Alnylam Pharmaceuticals. The project features a high-performance facade, energy-efficient systems, and a rooftop garden.

Assembly Innovation Park is a 12-story, 485,000 square foot life science tower located in Assembly Square, Somerville. The project is part of a larger master plan that will include residential, retail, and office space. The building is designed to achieve LEED Gold certification and features a robust amenity package.
